**EXACT EDIT TEXT**: NEW §6.7H starting at original line 2854 (now ~2854+50). Contents:
 (1) Keyword anchors at top — 8 anchors including 'dbt docs generate serve', 'dbt model description', 'dbt column description', 'where to write dbt descriptions', 'dbt doc blocks {% docs %}', 'dbt documentation site', 'catalog.json manifest.json', 'reuse dbt description across models'.
 (2) Verified-sources line: docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/documentation + docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/cmd-docs.
 (3) WHERE descriptions live — schema YAML file with `description:` key on model AND each column under `columns:`; also works on sources/seeds/snapshots/macros. **Explicit DO-NOT: descriptions do NOT go inline in `.sql` file.**
 (4) LONG-FORM / REUSABLE doc blocks — `{% docs my_block %} ... markdown ... {% enddocs %}` in any `.md` file under model paths; reference from YAML via `description: "{{ doc('my_block') }}"`. Use case: reuse one description across many columns + richer markdown than YAML one-liner.
 (5) GENERATE + SERVE — `dbt docs generate` builds `manifest.json` (project graph/metadata) + `catalog.json` (column types/stats, queried from warehouse information_schema). `dbt docs serve` runs local HTML site on default port 8080. On-prem k8s alternative: host generated static files behind nginx.
 (6) Worked YAML example — `models/marts/_schema.yml` with `version: 2`, one model `fct_orders` with `description:` + 2 columns, each with own `description:`, third column showing `{{ doc('order_total_cents') }}` to demonstrate the doc-block reference.
 (7) DO-NOT-WRITE table — 4 banned patterns: (a) inline `-- description:` SQL comments expecting them in docs site (WRONG LOCATION — dbt only scrapes YAML + .md docs blocks), (b) claiming `dbt docs generate` runs/materializes models (WRONG — only compiles metadata + queries information_schema), (c) confusing dbt docs with source freshness (§6.7B → target/sources.json) or contracts (§6.7C → schema enforcement), (d) `{% docs %}` block in a `.sql` file (WRONG FILE TYPE — must be `.md`).

Total: ~52 lines, slightly above the 14-line guideline because the gap covers 4 distinct mechanisms (where descriptions live, doc blocks, generate/serve, banned patterns) and the worked YAML example is the most important keyword-anchor for 'how do I document my dbt model'. All 4 mechanisms are mandatory per the directive's scope spec.

**WEBSEARCH VERIFICATION**: (1) `dbt docs generate` confirmed at docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/cmd-docs — creates `target/manifest.json` + `target/catalog.json`; `catalog.json` populated by querying warehouse `information_schema` for column types/row counts. `dbt docs serve` runs on default port 8080. (2) `description:` mechanism confirmed at docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/documentation — descriptions live in schema YAML files (under `models:`, `columns:`, also `sources:`, `seeds:`, `snapshots:`, `macros:`), NOT in `.sql` files. (3) Doc blocks confirmed: `{% docs name %} ... {% enddocs %}` syntax, must be in `.md` files, referenced via `doc('name')` Jinja function (analogous to `ref()`), works only in description fields of resource YAML properties (models, columns, sources, source tables, source columns). (4) `manifest.json` vs `catalog.json` distinction confirmed: manifest = full repo of project resources + nodal config + resource properties; catalog = warehouse-derived view/table info including column types + row counts. All examples in edit are valid dbt-trino YAML / Jinja.
